human_tolerance.notes: 'Common in residential areas', and it eats 'scraps in town parks, bird-table food'. It is frequently subordinate at feeders to gray squirrels, scrub jays, grackles and red-headed woodpeckes, which are occasionally observed to prevent jays feeding altogether. Its westwards range expansion followed fire suppression and tree planting.

phases.name: breeding
phases.note: Window is authored judgement: the source gives the breeding biology but no calendar dates. Pairs build together, the female alone broods, the male feeds her on the nest, and three to six eggs (usually four or five) are incubated over 16-18 days.

phases.name: nesting
phases.note: An open cup of twigs, grass, paper and feathers built in the branches of a tree; the young fledge 17-21 days after hatching, and the family then travels and forages together until early fall.

phases.name: dispersal
phases.note: Young birds disperse in early fall to avoid competition for food over winter; some adults disperse too.

phases.name: absent
phases.note: The northernmost subspecies is migratory where necessary and may withdraw several hundred kilometres south; thousands pass in loose daytime flocks along the Great Lakes and Atlantic coasts.

phases.name: flocking
phases.note: Migrating birds travel in loose flocks of 5 to 250.

vocalizations.description: A varied jay song, of quiet conversational notes including the squeaky 'rusty pump' phrase, used between jays in company. Corvids are distinct from most other songbirds in using such calls as their song.
The most recognized sound: a loud, almost gull-like scream. Given by individuals and by groups driving off potential predators such as hawks near the nest.
A high-pitched 'jayer-jayer' call that speeds up as the bird becomes more agitated; easy to confuse with a chickadee's 'chick-ah-dee-ee'.
Copies the cries of local hawks so well that it is sometimes hard to tell which bird is calling; individual jays also learn to mimic human speech.

external.note: eBird code blujay via Wikipedia's infobox.

range.note: Southern Canada and the eastern and central United States south to Florida and northeastern Texas; a rare but regular winter visitor now along the northern US and southern Canadian Pacific coast after a twentieth-century westward expansion. Not treated as introduced anywhere.

traits.locomotion_modes.note: Gleans food from trees, shrubs and the ground and perches; the shared perching-songbird program forages on the ground by hops, which is how this ground-feeding corvid moves.

traits.perching.note: Gleans from trees and shrubs, perches conspicuously, and raises and flattens its crest according to mood.

traits.senses.note: The article describes strong vocal learning: copying hawks so closely that the two are hard to tell apart, and learning human speech. That supports High hearing. Olfaction is set to Med as a mid-range default for a corvid rather than from a source claim, and vision_colour is omitted because the article attributes the blue to feather structure rather than describing colour vision.

traits.mass_kg.note: Midpoint of Wikipedia's 70-100 g range; the article's Connecticut mean of 92.4 g and Florida mean of 73.7 g both fall inside it.

traits.length_m.note: Midpoint of Wikipedia's 22-30 cm bill-to-tail length.

traits.lifespan_y.note: 'A more common lifespan for wild birds that survive to adulthood is around 7 years.'

traits.diet.note: The Audubon estimate that '75% of their diet is vegetable matter' sets the plant share, split across the plant items the article names - acorns and beech mast, weed seeds, grain, and fruit and other berries - as mast 0.3, seed 0.25 and fruit 0.2. The remaining 25% is recorded as invertebrate 0.2 with vertebrate 0.05 for the 'occasionally small vertebrates' and 'rarely eggs and nestlings' the article mentions.

traits.social.note: 'Blue jays typically form monogamous pair bonds for life', and the family forages together until the young disperse in early fall.

traits.activity_pattern.note: Diurnal: it 'migrates during the daytime' and gleans in daylight.

traits.defense.note: It 'can be very aggressive to other birds', mobs hawks with the 'jay jayer' call to drive them from the nest, and appropriates the nests of other mid-sized songbirds.

traits.wariness.note: Judgement: 0.4. Comfortable in residential areas and at bird tables, but often gives way at feeders to squirrels and larger birds, and it flushes readily when a person comes close in a nesting tree.

habitat.use.note: The ground share follows the article's 'its food is sought both on the ground and in trees'; the arboreal share covers gleaning from the canopy, nest building in branches and perching. The article gives no quantified stratum split, so this is judgement.

habitat.shelter_tag.note: The article notes the bird appropriates the nests of other mid-sized songbirds such as American robins, and will nest in almost any site if nothing better is available.

habitat.resources.note: Food weights follow traits.diet. Nesting weight is on the open cup in tree branches, which the host places with nest_cup; cavity is recorded as the shelter tag because it reuses other birds' nests. perch and shrub_thicket are shelter, weighted by judgement.

habitat.human_tolerance.note: It is 'common in residential areas' and takes 'scraps in town parks, bird-table food'. The account of being dominated at feeders by gray squirrels, scrub jays, grackles and red-headed woodpeckes sets the social end of the tolerance scale. impervious_max, flight_distance_m and road_mortality are authored judgement and are not quantified in the source; West Nile virus is noted as a major mortality factor but is a disease, not a road effect.

habitat.density_per_ha.note: Judgement: the article reports a mixed trend - a decline along the Atlantic coast from 1966 to 2015 but greater than 1.5% annual growth across the northern range - without a population density. A territorial pair on roughly 2 ha gives typical 0.5 per hectare, and min and max are an authored tenfold band either side, following the convention used for turdus-migratorius and cardinalis-cardinalis.

seasonal.strategy.note: 'Some eastern populations may be migratory' and 'the northernmost subspecies ... is, subject to necessity, migratory', while 'some are present throughout winter in all parts of their range'.

seasonal.winter_fraction.note: Judgement: set at 0.6 to reflect a partial migrant whose southern and central range birds are largely resident, with the northernmost subspecies withdrawing where necessary.

seasonal.phases.note: Pair bonds, both sexes building, female-only brooding, male feeding the female, three to six eggs (usually four or five) over 16-18 days, fledging at 17-21 days, family association to early fall, dispersal, the partial withdrawal of the northernmost subspecies and the loose daytime flocks of 5 to 250 are all from the article. The calendar windows are authored judgement because the article gives no dates.

seasonal.life_stages.note: Juvenile duration is authored: fledging at 17-21 days plus the one to two months young 'may stay with their parents', rounded to 120 days, and sexual maturity is 'reached after one year of age'. scale is authored judgement.

vocalizations.note: The gull-like scream alarm, the speeding 'jayer-jayer' call and its confusion with chickadee, the 'rusty pump' conversational call, hawk mimicry, speech mimicry and the corvid use of a call as song all come from the Vocalizations section. Time windows and cooldowns are authored judgement; no open source quantifies them. No open source gives frequency bands, so freq_hz is omitted.

look.note: Colours from the lead and Description: lavender-blue to mid-blue crest, back, wings and tail, white face, off-white underside, a black collar round the neck extending to the sides of the head, strongly barred black and sky-blue wing primaries and tail, and black bill, legs and eyes. The blue is structural rather than pigment, which is why the palette uses two related blues for body and crest. Proportions are authored judgement for a long-tailed, crested corvid with a heavy bill.

behavior.note: Authored parameters for the shared perching-songbird program. flee_m raised to 12 m for a large, bold bird that mobs threats instead of fleeing them; food_tag is mast because acorns and beech mast are the staple it cracks with its bill; song and alarm are the two calls the program drives and both are named above; nest_m1 and nest_m2 follow the program's declared params and the article's 'in the branches of a tree'.
